pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to King's Academy Meadow Vale
pageCache.text:
Delivering Opportunity & Success on a Global Stage
A family of academies shaping futures through education, ambition and community.
Welcome to King's Academy Meadow Vale
Our Values & Ethos
Honesty means telling the truth even when it’s difficult, and admitting when I’ve got something wrong. It helps me learn from my mistakes and means people can trust what I say.
Faith means believing that I can improve, even when maths feels tricky at first. It helps me keep trying and trust that practice will help me get there.
Reading, Writing & Maths
Courage means not giving up, even when a test feels hard. Being brave helps me keep going and try my best, no matter the result.
Opportunity & Success on a Global Stage
Through our International Dimension, we connect students and staff with schools across the world, creating meaningful collaboration, wider perspectives and new ambitions for the future.
Latest News & Socials
Oakleaf Newsletter - Issue 117
Oakleaf Newsletter - Issue 116

Oakleaf Newsletter - Issue 113
A reminder for Year 1 and 2 parents. Great Fire of London day on Monday 21st Spetember. Please remember to dress up and bring in a cereal box.
🎒✨ Welcome back! ✨🎒 We hope everyone has had a wonderful summer break! We’re so excited to welcome our pupils and families back for another fantastic year filled with learning, laughter and lots of exciting opportunities. 📚💛 Here’s to a brilliant year ahead! 🌟 Remember school starts at 8:50am tomorrow morning!
🌟 We're proud to share some fantastic news! 🌟 King's Academy Meadow Vale has been awarded the English Hubs Sustained Excellence Award in recognition of our continued commitment to high-quality phonics and early reading. This award reflects the incredible dedication of our staff, who work hard every day to ensure every child has the best possible start to their reading journey. From carefully planned phonics lessons and targeted support to creating a love of reading across the school, this achievement is a testament to their passion and commitment. We are incredibly proud of what our staff have achieved and would like to thank our families for their ongoing support. Together, we are helping our children become confident, enthusiastic and successful readers. Well done to everyone involved! 📚🎉
Reception had a fantastic time at Bocketts Farm Park! After a visit to the barn, small animal encounters, a tractor ride, piglet races and lots of water breaks, the children made the most of their time at the playbarn.
Yesterday, year 5 and 6 had the opportunity to attend oasis sessions run by volunteers from local churches. It provided the children a moment of calm and reflection on the year as well as the upcoming changes ahead of them. They all particularly enjoyed sitting in the hugging chair to have a moment of peace. Thank you to Judy and all the volunteers for providing our children with this wonderful session!
Reception had a lot of fun comparing the stories of We're Going on a Bear Hunt and We're Going on a Lion Hunt. The children had their own fantastic ideas for an adventure they would each like to go on...
Immersed in their learning about Africa, Reception used clay to create their own designs of African masks. Little artists in the making! 🥰
5A kicked off our International Week by exploring the 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Our first challenge was to work silently to order the 17 goals from most to least important—a real test of teamwork, communication without words and critical thinking! Next, the children worked in groups to design their own country, using their top three SDGs as the foundation and exploring how they would affect their country. They then had the exciting task of convincing their classmates why they should choose to live in their country. There were some incredibly creative ideas and thoughtful discussions about what makes a country a great place to live. We are looking forward to another exciting day of learning tomorrow as our International Week continues! 🌎✨
Whilst our Year 6 children were visiting their new secondary schools, those still in school spent time supporting our FS children. The Year 6 buddies did a wonderful job and the younger children loved spending time with them. 🙂‍📖
🏺 Ancient Greek Pot Making 🏺 6M worked incredibly hard while exploring Ancient Greek pot making! They carefully handled the modelling clay to create their own Ancient Greek pots, using sculpting tools to smooth the surface before adding lots of intricate details with great care and creativity. We are so proud of their focus, perseverance and fantastic craftsmanship. Well done, 6M! 👏✨
🚍Bude update🚍 Both coaches have swapped drivers and are now on our way to Bracknell! Our new ETA is 5:20pm. We look forward to seeing you shortly!☀️😊
🚌 Bude update 🚌 We are now back on the road and hope to be back at school at 5:45. We will provide an update after we have swapped drivers at Reading services. Thank you for your patience and we look forward to seeing you soon! ☀️
A fantastic time at the PTA Summer Fair last Friday. The turnout was amazing and we thank you all for your amazing donations! ☀
The children have all had a brilliant first day of activities in Bude! 🌊🛶 Photos of the trip so far will be added to the website tomorrow. ☺️
☀️Bude 2026☀️ We have arrived safely and all children have found their rooms and are now enjoying the sun! Ready for a fantastic week of activity 🌊
4W have been creating safety posters for school children living in earthquake prone areas. We discussed the 3 P's: prediction, protection and preparation and compiled some top tips to keep others safe.
6D had a brilliant time cooking on Tuesday! They worked hard to create their own pasta dish and fruit salad. Everyone enjoyed their final dish! 🍜👩🏽‍🍳👨🏾‍🍳
A reminder for Year 6 parents! The weather is looking great and we can't wait for this years residential! ☀️🌊 If you have any further questions, please speak to your child's class teacher.

Pastoral
Gold Accreditation
A big well done to all staff, pupils, and families for a whole school contribution towards gaining a gold accreditation on our OPAL journey in October 2025. To keep up to date with all things OPAL, please do read the monthly newsletters that can be found further down the page.
Download the OPAL introduction letter
What is OPAL?
Research has shown that children spend 20% of their time in school playing. To ensure that this time and our fantastic school grounds are used to their full potential, our school has adopted an OPAL (Outdoor Play and Learning) philosophy that allows the children freedom to explore play in their own imaginative ways, often using found and gathered resources in the natural outdoor environment as well as made-made items.
We believe that play is essential for the physical, emotional, social, spiritual and intellectual development of each child. An OPAL approach promotes a more inclusive play environment in which all children can feel comfortable expressing themselves. Most of our best childhood memories are from playing outdoors, climbing trees and exploring the wide world around us. OPAL gives us the opportunity to give those memories to your children. OPAL's mission statement is "To ensure that every schoolchild has an amazing playtime every day with no exceptions."
Improve well-being
Develop self-regulation
Increase physical activity
Aid social and emotional development
Learn to manage risk
Have FUN!
Why OPAL?
The OPAL Programme rationale is that:
“More active and creative playtimes can mean happier and healthier children, and having happier, healthier, more active children usually results in a more positive attitude to learning in school, with more effective classroom lessons, less staff time spent resolving unnecessary behavioural problems, fewer playtime accidents, happier staff and a healthier attitude to life”.
Since starting our journey to enrich playtimes in 2023, we have begun to develop our vision of play across the school and are listening to feedback from children, families and staff. The children love the new outdoor opportunities that OPAL offers, including exploring the tyres, dancing to music and learning about the wildlife in the pond area. As we continue to introduce more activities, children are not only more active at playtimes, but they are also having the opportunity to further develop life skills such as cooperation, teamwork and problem-solving. They are becoming motivated and enthusiastic builders, engineers, explorers and artists.
Thank you
As part of our OPAL journey, one of the favourite things our pupils enjoy is whizzing around on their scooters and bikes. Our younger pupils have progressed from three wheels to two wheels and some of our older pupils are mastering tricks whilst assessing their own risk.
We recently invested in more scooters, and we would like to give a huge thank you to Micro Scooters for donating helmets to ensure the safety of our pupils. Their line-up includes toddler scooters, adult scooters, and plenty of models in between.
Check out our monthly newsletters below to keep up to date with all things OPAL.
To support our ongoing play projects, are you able to donate any of the following:
Please place any donations in the OPAL box found in the front office area. Thank you!
You can find our OPAL Play Policy in our Policies and documents section of the website.
Please see the attachment below for the play assemblies we share with the children. We use these to celebrate positive play, introduce new resources, and discuss how we can safely manage our own risks.

Welcome from the Headteacher
Welcome to King's Academy Meadow Vale
On behalf of the children, staff and governors, welcome to our school's website!
King's Academy Meadow Vale is a large, three-form entry primary school in Bracknell with our own nursery class.
Our school enjoys an excellent reputation within our local community because of our hard-working staff team who strive to ensure that every child is encouraged to develop their potential through a stimulating, challenging and relevant curriculum. We are very proud of our school, have high expectations of what we can achieve together and value the significant contribution that parents and carers make to their child’s education.
We have outstanding facilities within our large school grounds, including an adventure playground, extensive grassed areas and a wide range of extracurricular activities.
I hope that you enjoy your visit to our website and that you find any information you are looking for. Please feel free to contact us through the school office with any queries you may have, or to arrange a viewing of our school.
I look forward to meeting you.

PTA and Volunteering
Welcome to the King's Academy Meadow Vale PTA
Comprising parents and carers, the PTA organises events to fundraise for the school. Our primary goal is to gather funds for resources and equipment that enrich our children's education.
Last year, the PTA raised funds through various events including fireworks, Christmas cards, movie nights, discos, and a summer fair. The success of these events was made possible by the fantastic support of our parent community, who contributed their time and presence. We are continually seeking new members who can bring fresh ideas or assist at our events. Participation in the PTA is not limited to committee members; anyone can offer help or attend meetings. It's an excellent opportunity to meet others, particularly for families new to the school.
The PTA plays a vital role in raising funds for the school, aiding in the purchase of items like scooters to use at lunchtime and supporting seasonal activities, such as the whole school's Christmas pantomime. We also contribute to teachers' requests for resources needed for after-school clubs.
Contact
For event tickets and other products: https://www.pta-events.co.uk/meadowvalepta/
For enquiries, suggestions, or if you wish to support the PTA, email us at: pta@meadowvaleprimary.com
You can also find us on Facebook: Meadow Vale School PTA
Committee members
Please do come and find us in the playground if you'd like to have a chat or get involved.

pageCache.pageTitle: School Lunch - King's Academy Meadow Vale
pageCache.text:
School Lunch
Menus
The current school meals menu is for Spring/Summer 2026.
Payment
School meals are provided by Aspens at a price of £2.53. Parents need to open an account for their child on SCOPAY and keep it in credit for school meals to be ordered daily. Click here for more information on Aspens, or to view the parent's guide, please click here.
Information about free school meal eligibility and how to apply can be found on the Bracknell Forest website.
Special dietary requirements
If your child has special dietary requirements, such as for medical, allergy, or cultural reasons, and receives school meals, please submit a special diet form.
Nut / peanut allergies
Please ensure that packed lunches do not contain any form of nuts/peanuts. This includes Nutella, peanut butter, chocolate/cereal bars containing nuts, and any other products that contain nuts. Whilst we appreciate this may cause an inconvenience, we have to consider the welfare of all children and have a duty of care for them. Thank you for your understanding of this matter.

pageCache.text:
Curriculum Overview
Curriculum Overview: King’s Academy Meadow Vale
At King’s Academy Meadow Vale (part of King’s Group Academies), the curriculum is built around the core vision of "Opportunity and Success on a Global Stage." It aims to nurture curious, confident, and compassionate young people who are empowered with both academic excellence and an international perspective. By embedding global citizenship, cultural connections—such as language spotlights and partner school links in Rwanda—and essential 21st-century skills directly into everyday learning, the school ensures that every pupil gains the knowledge, resilience, and ambition required to thrive in an interconnected modern world.
Core Subject Areas & Learning Pathways
English & Phonics: A structured, high-quality literacy pathway focusing on phonics, reading fluency, vocabulary acquisition, and creative writing. Knowledge organisers and recommended reading lists support deep comprehension across all year groups.
Mathematics: A mastery-driven approach designed to build numerical fluency, logical reasoning, and problem-solving through concrete, pictorial, and abstract methods.
Science: Practical, enquiry-based learning covering core concepts in biology, chemistry, and physics. Pupils develop investigation techniques, evidence evaluation, and analytical thinking.
Computing: Digital literacy, internet safety, and foundational coding principles that empower pupils to navigate technology safely and responsibly.
History & Geography: Local, national, and global topic studies that teach historical chronology and geographical awareness while encouraging pupils to reflect on how past events and human activity shape today's world.
Religious Education (RE): Exploration of world religions, diverse worldviews, and ethical questions to promote open-mindedness, empathy, and respect.
Arts & Music: Expressive arts designed to foster individual creativity, performance confidence, and artistic exploration.
Physical Education & OPAL Play: Structured PE along with Outdoor Play and Learning (OPAL) initiatives to support physical health, teamwork, leadership, and emotional wellbeing.
Remote education provision
We are committed to ensuring that every child can continue their learning journey, even when they are unable to attend school in person. Our remote education provision will be tailored to meet the needs of the children and may include a blend of live lessons, recorded activities, use of online resources, and independent learning tasks designed to reflect our in-school curriculum as far as practicable. Teachers will provide regular feedback and support to help pupils stay motivated, make progress, and remain connected to their classmates. We use a range of accessible online platforms that are easy for both children and parents to navigate, ensuring a smooth and engaging learning experience for all.
When a child may need to be educated remotely
Remote education may be provided when a pupil is unable to attend school in person but is well enough to continue learning from home; this provision will be reviewed regularly. This could include situations such as short-term illness, recovery from injury, reintegration back into school, exclusion, or exceptional family circumstances (in agreement with and authorised by the headteacher) where attending school is not possible. It may be used in the event of a temporary school or class closure. Our aim is to ensure that all pupils can continue to make progress and remain connected to their class.
How remote learning is delivered
Our remote education will be provided through Google Classroom. Each class has its own online space where teachers can upload lessons, activities, and resources. Children may be able to join live sessions, watch recorded lessons, complete assignments, and receive personalised feedback from their teacher. Parents and carers are supported with guidance on how to help their child access learning and printed materials or digital devices may be provided for families who need them. Agreed home visits from members of staff will form part of the remote education provision offer. This approach ensures every pupil stays engaged, supported and connected to their school community.
